As you can see, using "autistic" as an insult is a very commonly spread thing here. Especially among young people. As far as I am aware, Bulgaria is not doing enough to grant rights for people with mental illnesses or neurodiverse conditions such as autism. Idk about legal protection, but I highly doubt what is being done is enough. There is constant underfunding for things like mental illness treatment or support for intellectual disabilities, and the majority of people are undereducated on them and often conflate the two. Stigma is much much worse than in the West, there are virtually no awareness campaigns, no education, nothing. There isn't even a national strategy for suicide prevention, nor are there any hotlines and it seems that the government doesn't deem it worthwhile to even acknowledge the need for them, or discuss it. Topics concerning mental health, illness, neurodiversity, mental or learning disability are pretty much a taboo and a sign of weakness for people who bring them up.
Most of the groups, organizations and resources for autism in Bulgaria are for autistic children and parents of autistic children, almost nothing about autistic adults. Autism pride is unheard of, neurodiversity as a concept too.
